subject: Bounding a parameter by another parameter in a hierarchical model.

messages.author: ad91bbac71425e94
messages.subject: Bounding a parameter by another parameter in a hierarchical model.
parts:
Hello,

I’m attempting to estimate a hierarchical double exponential mixture model (two shifted exponetials, actually). The model is fitted to inter-response times of rats, where the inter-response times of each rat are fit to the double-exponential, and the parameters of the double exponential are assumed to be log-normally distributed at the group level.

I’ve gotten the non-hierarchical version of the model to work, however, the bounding of parameters is giving me some trouble in the hierarchical model. One parameter (pW0) can never be smaller than another (pB0).

In the non-hierarchical case, it’s a simple matter of:

real<lower=pB0,upper=positive_infinity()> pW0;

However, in the hierarchical case, pW0 and pB0 are vectors (one value for each rat).  How can I set the bounds so that the lower bound of pW0 for each rat is that rat’s pB0?

For-loops don’t seem to work in the parameter designation area, giving the following error:

EXPECTATION FAILURE LOCATION: file=input; line=16, column=3

  for (r in 1:rat_count) {

  ^-- here

DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:

Parser expecting: "}">

 Similarly, the parameter that shifts the distribution of response times, pDelta, should be constrained so that it can never be larger than the smallest response time (min_irt) for each animal. However, I have similar problem deciding how to write the code where each individual minimum response time serves as the upper bounds for each individual’s pDelta.

I suspect there’s a simple trick using vectors that I’m unaware of. If anyone could offer some advice, I’d greatly appreciate it!

I’ve attached the model and R script, along with sample data files.

-Ryan

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Bounding a parameter by another parameter in a hierarchical model.
parts:
Dan's suggestion is the only one that'll work --- Stan
doesn't support (yet) vectors of upper-and-lower bounds
constraints.

You're not the first person to ask for this.
What I'd like to support is declarations like this:

vector<lower=L,upper=U>[N] x;

where L is an N-vector of lower bounds and U an N-vector
of upper bounds. This would be a pretty straightforward
addition. You could even vectorize so that either L or U
could also be a scalar, with the intention that it replicate
out to size N.

- Bob

Thanks for the suggestion, Dan. The reparametrization works great, though I'm still in a bind for pDelta, where I need to constrain the upper bound by a different value for each subject. Without the constraint, the observations can dip past zero, which causes everything else to fall apart. 

I've been experimenting with ways to get around the programming constraint, but without success. If anyone has a suggestions, I'd be extremely grateful.

Bob - I'm excited to see vectored LB and UB are coming eventually. Stan seems like fantastic project. I'm amazed at how involved the developers are with the community. 

Thanks,
Ryan

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Bounding a parameter by another parameter in a hierarchical model.
parts:
On 10/11/13 8:21 PM, Ryan Brackney wrote:
> Thanks for the suggestion, Dan. The reparametrization works great, though I'm still in a bind for pDelta, where I need
> to constrain the upper bound by a different value for each subject. Without the constraint, the observations can dip
> past zero, which causes everything else to fall apart.
>
> I've been experimenting with ways to get around the programming constraint, but without success. If anyone has a
> suggestions, I'd be extremely grateful.

You can just follow the transformations defined in the
transformation section of the manual. We use a scaled and
translated inv_logit for going from (-inf,inf) to (L,U).
The Jacobian's pretty simple here and fully documented in
the transformation section.

Sorry it's such a pain now. This is a use case we
really didn't anticipate.

> Bob - I'm excited to see vectored LB and UB are coming eventually. Stan seems like fantastic project. I'm amazed at how
> involved the developers are with the community.

We're trying. It's enormously helpful for us because
we want to make something usable. And we really want to understand
how HMC and NUTS work. I hope that one of our contributions is
evaluating HMC on so many different sizes and shapes of models.

- Bob
